root_cause.text: The iwlwifi MLD code failed to cancel the per-vif delayed work `mlo_scan_start_wk` during station teardown/disconnection in `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()`, leaving queued work able to run after `drv_change_interface` or after the `vif` was freed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly says "`mlo_scan_start_wk` is not canceled on disconnection" and warns this "can cause an init-after-queue issue" and "use-after-free"; the patch adds `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk);` in `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()` and removes the only previous cancellation from later restart cleanup in `iwl_mld_cleanup_vif()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove explicit cancellation of mlo_scan_start_wk from vif cleanup to avoid incorrect work handling during cleanup.
intent_record.what: The call to wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk); was removed from iwl_mld_cleanup_vif(), leaving the key iteration and CLEANUP_STRUCT(mld_vif) cleanup steps intact.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer cancels the mlo_scan_start_wk delayed work when cleaning up a vif, so that work is now left to be canceled elsewhere or allowed to follow its existing lifecycle instead of being explicitly stopped here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending mlo_scan_start_wk during STA state teardown to prevent deferred scan work from running after the state goes down.
intent_record.what: A call to wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(mld->wiphy, &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk) was added in iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down() alongside existing cancellations of other pending work items during station state teardown.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the delayed mlo_scan_start_wk work is canceled when the STA state is moved down, preventing that deferred scan-start task from running after the interface/state has been torn down or transitioned, which avoids stale asynchronous execution.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant teardown logic is fully visible in `iwl_mld_move_sta_state_down()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause says the bug is failure to cancel the per-vif delayed work `mlo_scan_start_wk` during station teardown/disconnection. In this function, for the station disconnect path `old_state == IEEE80211_STA_AUTHORIZED && new_state == IEEE80211_STA_ASSOC`, it cancels several per-vif works: `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(... &mld_vif->emlsr.prevent_done_wk);`, `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(... &mld_vif->emlsr.tmp_non_bss_done_wk);`, `wiphy_work_cancel(... &mld_vif->emlsr.unblock_tpt_wk);`, and `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(... &mld_vif->emlsr.check_tpt_wk);`. However, there is no cancellation of `mlo_scan_start_wk` anywhere in this teardown/disconnection function, including the later teardown path `old_state == IEEE80211_STA_NONE && new_state == IEEE80211_STA_NOTEXIST` where it only does `iwl_mld_remove_sta(mld, sta);`. Since the vulnerable construct is precisely the omission of `wiphy_delayed_work_cancel(... &mld_vif->mlo_scan_start_wk)` (or equivalent) during station teardown, the bug is present and the fix is not present.
